evidence_summary.headline: Recommended: Outcome-based revision (-6.0% modeled delay). Largest modeled reduction: Add arterial lane (capacity experiment) (-49.8%), not eligible: Capital $1,200,000 exceeds the $100,000 budget.
observed_facts: 77 City-reported incidents at Deerfoot Trail & Glenmore Trail SE over 184 days (12.7 per month).
56 (73%) blocked at least one lane; 23 of those started in a weekday peak period.
28 (36%) are 'Traffic incident' with no stated cause.
40 collisions, 0 involving a pedestrian or cyclist, 0 signal faults.
Incident weighting used in the comparison: 8.7% of peak windows (lane-blocking peak incidents / observed weekday peak periods).
Modeled cost of one 20-min incident: +82.7 s per vehicle (40.7 vehicle-hours in the study window).

options.label: Demand-based retiming
options.sentence: Demand-based retiming: modeled delay +24.4% vs the reference, cross streets +58.0%, $15,000 assumed capital. During incidents it adds 45.0 vehicle-hours per event; at the 23 peak lane-blocking incidents seen in six months that is about 1035 vehicle-hours added (modeled). Not eligible: Cross-street delay +58% exceeds the 30% limit.

options.label: Outcome-based revision
options.sentence: Outcome-based revision: modeled delay -6.0% vs the reference, cross streets +0.2%, $15,000 assumed capital. During incidents it adds 0.2 vehicle-hours per event; at the 23 peak lane-blocking incidents seen in six months that is about 6 vehicle-hours added (modeled).

options.label: Add arterial lane (capacity experiment)
options.what: An extra arterial lane in each direction
options.sentence: An extra arterial lane in each direction: modeled delay -49.8% vs the reference, cross streets -44.3%, $1,200,000 assumed capital. During incidents it saves 75.4 vehicle-hours per event; at the 23 peak lane-blocking incidents seen in six months that is about 1734 vehicle-hours saved (modeled). Not eligible: Capital $1,200,000 exceeds the $100,000 budget.

During incidents it adds 0.1 vehicle-hours per event; at the 23 peak lane-blocking incidents seen in six months that is about 3 vehicle-hours added (modeled).

evidence_summary.proof_standard: City records show where and how often disruptions occur; they do not measure delay. Improvements are modeled on a synthetic corridor using those records (demand from 2024 volumes, incident frequency/lanes). Field effect needs calibrated counts and engineering review.
